landing.faq.items.0.answer: Start with a short excerpt saved as its own EPUB, PDF or TXT file, or use a sample story in the studio. Full manuscripts are supported, but a smaller first project helps you assess the result and credit use before expanding.
landing.faq.items.0.question: What should I start with?
landing.faq.items.1.answer: Yes. You approve the story, look and cast, then review complete page revisions and decide which page issues to correct or accept as-is.
landing.faq.items.1.question: Can I change what it makes?
landing.faq.items.2.answer: No generative system can promise perfect continuity. Scenewright improves it with approved character references, location plates and book-level story state, then lets you correct complete pages that miss.
landing.faq.items.2.question: Will every character look perfectly identical?
landing.faq.items.3.answer: You retain ownership of your manuscript. Scenewright claims no ownership over generated output, though purely generated images may not qualify for copyright protection in every jurisdiction.
landing.faq.items.3.question: Who owns the manuscript and output?
landing.faq.items.4.answer: Yes. Third-party generative models assist with adaptation and illustration. The workflow keeps the author in charge of the key choices, edits and final arrangement.
landing.faq.items.4.question: Does Scenewright use AI?
landing.faq.items.5.answer: There is no subscription. Credit packs start at US$12, credits never expire, and Scenewright estimates each paid step before it runs. Total use depends on length, quality and revisions.
